channel.title: L'Esclop
channel.description: New versions of L'Esclop, written by Scripts/appcast.sh.

item.title: L'Esclop 0.1.1
item.description:
Preset zones beside the drop zone, uploads to your own S3-compatible storage, and a PDF engine of L'Esclop's own in place of Ghostscript. 0.1.0 installs this update by itself.
### Added - Preset zones: while files are dragged, up to four targets beside the drop zone, in a 2 × 2 grid facing the screen, each running a pipeline on what is dropped on it, through the usual floating results or the batch window. A saved pipeline is one when its triggers include "A preset zone while dragging"; the built-in templates are turned on in Settings › Floating results › Preset zones, which also orders them all. A drag shows the first four that do something for every kind of file in it. `esclop://dropzone` shows the drop zone without a drag for a minute (`?kind=image|video|pdf|audio` for that kind's zones, `?hide` to hide it). The drop zone's text and icons now use the popover's explicit inks. - Uploads: after optimising, upload the result to your own S3-compatible storage (AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, MinIO) and get its link on the clipboard. From a result's Share tab ("Upload to …"), from a pipeline step (`upload(to: "R2")`), automatically for the sources you choose (copied files, the drop zone, watched folders, Finder's Quick Actions), with `esclop upload` and with the MCP tool `esclop_upload`. Targets are set up in Settings › Uploads (endpoint, bucket, region, path template, public link template, Test Upload); their keys are kept in the Keychain only, never in the settings, logs, `esclop settings` or MCP output, and only the app reads them: the command line and agents upload through it. An upload takes its turn with the other jobs, shows its progress on the result, can be stopped, and on failure keeps the file, says why and offers Upload Again. Agents may upload only when "Agents may upload files" (`allowUploads`, off by default) is on. - Agents' uploads and pipelines' upload steps take only images, videos, PDFs and audio whose first bytes (at most 4 KB are read) show the kind their extension names: a key or a text file renamed to `.png`, `.mp4`, `.pdf` or `.mp3` is refused, while a PNG named `.jpg` goes through. Uploads the person starts are not checked.
### Changed - PDFs are optimised by esclop-engine's `pdf.optimise` instead of Ghostscript: streams recompressed, images re-encoded and downsampled only where a fidelity check (SSIM at 150 dpi) passes, embedded TrueType and CFF fonts subset with their glyph ids kept (fonts a form field types with stay whole), large inline images moved to shared objects, unused objects dropped. Text, links, outlines, form fields and permissions stay as they were; JPEGs are re-encoded only when downsampled, and "Strip metadata" touches no image. Encrypted PDFs are re-encrypted with the same keys and permissions or left alone (and always left alone over 64 MB); signed and Reader-extended PDFs, damaged files and ones that would need more than 256 MB of memory besides their own size are left as they are, and the result says why. A PDF still being optimised 30 minutes after it started (time spent waiting behind others does not count) is stopped. On 1,576 real PDFs (the pdf.js test files and GovDocs) the engine failed none of the checks, where Ghostscript failed 506 at the default setting; on the files Ghostscript handled cleanly, the engine's output is 0.98x Ghostscript's at the default setting and 1.01x at the aggressive one. Its memory stays under 512 MB per file. See `engine/bench/pdf/RESULTS.md`.
### Removed - Ghostscript is no longer bundled (32 MB): the bundled tools go from 96 MB to 76 MB (universal). Scripts in pipelines that called `$ESCLOP_BIN/gs` need a Ghostscript of their own.
